result: {"findings": [{"file": "examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig", "line": 78, "severity": "minor", "category": "correctness", "title": "The socketpair close defer is now registered after a fallible operation, so a cancel leaks two descriptors per generation", "body": "Before this change the driver registered `defer _ = std.c.close(fds[0]); defer _ = std.c.close(fds[1]);` immediately after `socketpair`, so both descriptors were released on every exit path. The change replaces them with a single `defer` block at line 85 that is declared AFTER the `try sh.feed_mu.lock()` at line 78. `zio.Mutex.lock` returns `Cancelable!void`, so if that lock returns `error.Canceled` the driver returns before the close defer is registered and both descriptors are leaked. The loop runs up to `generations` (default 20000) times, so a driver cancelled repeatedly leaks two fds per generation and can exhaust the process fd table, which then makes `socketpair` fail and the repro report `error.SocketPair` instead of its real result. Register the close defer directly after the successful `socketpair` call (it does not need the mutex), and keep only the `feed_fd = -1` clear under the lock."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 11, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The stated harness contract accepts a bare SIGABRT, which the failure this death test exists to catch also produces", "body": "The new header states: \"A harness accepts only that abort (SIGABRT, or the message).\" SIGABRT alone is not a discriminating oracle here. The doc comment itself says the pre-claims failure surfaced \"as a `getResult` assert far from the cause\" - that assert is `std.debug.assert`, which also aborts with SIGABRT in Debug and ReleaseSafe. `driver` calls `c.cast(zio.ev.Async).getResult()` on every completion, so that exact assert is reachable in this example. A harness that matches on the signal alone therefore reports PASS for the corrupted-claim-accounting failure it was written to detect. The panic message is the only signal that separates the two outcomes, so the contract must require the message, not offer it as an alternative. No harness exists in this tree either, so nothing in `zig build` enforces the exit-3-means-fail rule that this change introduces."}, {"file": "examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig", "line": 24, "severity": "minor", "category": "docs", "title": "The reproduction-window claim in the header describes the old lock-free flooder and was not re-validated after the mutex was added", "body": "Lines 24-30 state the repro fires \"within ~1 s on macOS/kqueue and Linux/io_uring, Debug and ReleaseSafe, with 8 workers\" and that \"1-2 workers run clean\". That measurement was taken with a flooder whose hot loop was one atomic load plus a `write`. The change puts a `zio.Mutex` acquisition in that loop, and on contention `Mutex.lockSlow` parks the flooder task in the mutex wait queue and wakes it through a `Waiter.signal`. The repro's whole subject is a publish-then-wake window in the select waiter machinery, and the timing of that window is what the quoted numbers describe. Adding a parking wait to the flooder changes the interleaving the repro depends on, so the header now asserts a result the current code has not been shown to produce. Either re-run the repro and restate the window, or state that the window is unverified for the mutex-guarded flooder."}]}
